---
title: "North Carolina General Elections (2016–2026)"
subtitle: "Statewide Top-of-Ticket Results and Voting Methods from NCSBE Data"
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)

# Read all six zipped NCSBE files and standardize 2016-2022's "One Stop" column name
zip_files <- sort(list.files("data", pattern = "\\.zip$", full.names = TRUE))

nc_results <- map(zip_files, \(f) {
  read_tsv(f, show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "unique_quiet") |>
    rename(any_of(c("Early Voting" = "One Stop"))) |>
    select(!starts_with("..."))
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(Year = year(mdy(`Election Date`)))

# Pick the highest-turnout partisan statewide contest in each election year
top_contests <- tribble(
  ~Year, ~`Contest Name`,                             ~Race_Label,
  2016,  "US PRESIDENT",                              "2016 President",
  2018,  "NC SUPREME COURT ASSOCIATE JUSTICE SEAT 1", "2018 NC Supreme Ct",
  2020,  "US PRESIDENT",                              "2020 President",
  2022,  "US SENATE",                                 "2022 US Senate",
  2024,  "US PRESIDENT",                              "2024 President",
  2026,  "US SENATE",                                 "2026 US Senate"
)

top_races <- nc_results |>
  inner_join(top_contests, by = c("Year", "Contest Name"))
```

## How North Carolinians Cast Their Ballots (2016–2026)

Data come from the [NC State Board of Elections historical precinct results](https://www.ncsbe.gov/results-data/election-results/historical-election-results-data). Using the highest-turnout partisan statewide race in each November general election, we can compare total turnout and voting methods over the past decade.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.8

method_totals <- top_races |>
  summarize(
    `Early Voting` = sum(`Early Voting`, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Election Day` = sum(`Election Day`, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Absentee by Mail` = sum(`Absentee by Mail`, na.rm = TRUE),
    Provisional = sum(Provisional, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = c(Year, Race_Label)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(`Early Voting`, `Election Day`, `Absentee by Mail`, Provisional),
    names_to = "Method",
    values_to = "Votes"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Method = fct_relevel(Method, "Provisional", "Absentee by Mail", "Election Day", "Early Voting")
  )

ggplot(method_totals, aes(x = factor(Year), y = Votes, fill = Method)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M")) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", guide = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  labs(
    title = "Early Voting Consistently Leads North Carolina General Election Turnout",
    subtitle = "Ballots cast in the top statewide partisan contest, 2016–2026",
    x = "Election Year",
    y = "Votes Cast (Millions)",
    fill = "Voting Method",
    caption = "Source: NC State Board of Elections (NCSBE)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

## Top-of-Ticket Statewide Results by Party

```{r}
party_summary <- top_races |>
  summarize(
    Total_Contest_Votes = sum(`Total Votes`, na.rm = TRUE),
    DEM_Votes = sum(`Total Votes`[`Choice Party` == "DEM"], na.rm = TRUE),
    REP_Votes = sum(`Total Votes`[`Choice Party` == "REP"], na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = c(Year, Race_Label)
  )

winners <- top_races |>
  summarize(Votes = sum(`Total Votes`, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(Year, Choice, `Choice Party`)) |>
  slice_max(Votes, n = 1, by = Year) |>
  mutate(Winner = paste0(Choice, " (", `Choice Party`, ")")) |>
  select(Year, Winner)

party_summary |>
  left_join(winners, by = "Year") |>
  arrange(desc(Year)) |>
  mutate(
    `DEM %` = percent(DEM_Votes / Total_Contest_Votes, accuracy = 0.1),
    `REP %` = percent(REP_Votes / Total_Contest_Votes, accuracy = 0.1),
    `DEM Votes` = comma(DEM_Votes),
    `REP Votes` = comma(REP_Votes),
    `Total Votes` = comma(Total_Contest_Votes)
  ) |>
  select(
    Contest = Race_Label,
    Winner,
    `DEM Votes`,
    `DEM %`,
    `REP Votes`,
    `REP %`,
    `Total Votes`
  ) |>
  kable()
```
